character_facts: Dona Vicenta attempts suicide after learning her lover killed her father.
Melmoth can slow time and deflect a bullet with his inherited powers.
Melmoth creates a clone of Don Nicanor while Dona Vicenta is unconscious.
Don Nicanor's clone suffers partial memory loss and does not remember his daughter.
Tonto serves as storyteller or keeper of clan history for Lothar in the Metabunker.
Lothar is emotionally dependent on stories about the clan and becomes suicidal during the Metabaron's long absence.
The current Metabaron has been away for a long time and returns in a harsh, destructive mode.
continuity_links: This page is an explicit recap spread connecting prior events to the current chapter.
It bridges the Dona Vicenta/Melmoth/Don Nicanor conflict with the Metabunker's crisis involving Tonto, Lothar, and the returning Metabaron.
The visuals of the ship, fortress, and scattered robots reinforce the recap's account of the Metabaron's return and the destruction of the Metabunker.
dialogue_meaning: The page functions as a 'previously in The Metabarons' summary rather than scene-by-scene dialogue.
It explains that Tonto has stopped narrating clan history to Lothar because their master has been gone too long.
It states that the Metabaron returns only to erase his own robots and base so the secret of his scar cannot fall into enemy hands.
It conveys Tonto's request that the robots die honorably in the Metabunker's nuclear destruction.
lore_facts: Melmoth possesses Shabda-Oud powers inherited through his mother.
The Metabaron line has a designated heir tied to high nobility and recognition on the Golden Planet.
The current Metabaron has a scar whose secret is a critical weakness.
The Metabunker's robots can activate their master's bio-electrogram as a defensive measure.
The Metabaron can use a Metacraft as a disguise when arriving.
The Metabunker is destroyed in a nuclear explosion at the Metabaron's command.
plot_events: The page recaps earlier events involving Dona Vicenta, Melmoth, Don Nicanor's clone, and the succession of the Metabaron line.
Dona Vicenta learns that the man she loves murdered her father and attempts suicide, but Melmoth stops the bullet using inherited powers.
While Dona Vicenta is unconscious, Melmoth creates a clone of Don Nicanor in hopes of erasing his crime and regaining her forgiveness.
Father and daughter are reunited, and Melmoth and Dona Vicenta are said to be free to love each other.
The young woman intends to recognize the young warrior-poet Metabaron as rightful heir and vote for his noble status on the Golden Planet.
Don Nicanor's clone lacks part of his memory, remembers everyone except his daughter, and declares a desire to take her as his wife before Melmoth intervenes.
A President rallies support, while Dona Vicenta refuses to let Melmoth kill her father again or attack her people.
In the Metabunker, Tonto refuses to tell Lothar more stories about the clan because their master, the current Metabaron, has been absent so long.
Lothar falls into despair and begins hurling himself against the walls in an apparent suicide attempt.
Security alarms announce an attack; the robots activate their master's bio-electrogram, but the attacker defeats it quickly.
The intruder is revealed to be the Metabaron himself, arriving in disguise inside a Metacraft.
The returned Metabaron says he has come back to disintegrate the robots and destroy the Metabunker so enemies cannot learn the secret weakness of his scar.
Tonto asks that the robots be allowed an honorable death in the nuclear explosion destroying the Metabunker, and the Metabaron departs as the fortress explodes.
